title: Aelius Donatus, Commentum Terenti — Commentary on Terence; Элий Донат, «Комментарий к Теренцию». Proposed unit: commentary on Adelphoe
author: Aelius Donatus (Jerome's teacher); surviving text is a later reassembly of excerpts
date: c. 350 CE; reassembled in late antiquity/early Middle Ages
size: Wessner, 2 vols (~1,000 pp.); est. 250k words; Heautontimorumenos commentary lost (estimate)
edition: Wessner, Teubner 1902–05 (public domain; Wessner d. 1933). Recent critical editions of the Andria and Eunuchus commentaries are copyrighted (BMCR 2018.02.10)
ru_evidence: Russian search found nothing; ru.wikipedia 'Элий Донат' lists only the Ars minor (Petrova 1999)
en_evidence: en.wikipedia: 'never been translated to English'; no translation found in searches
other_translations: Partial German translation (per en.wikipedia); no complete modern translation found
value: Main ancient source on Roman comic staging, delivery, gesture and character, on colloquial Latin and on Menander (Greek comparisons). Used by theatre historians, Latinists, Menander scholars, and students of Renaissance comic theory
ai_feasibility: medium-high — short lemmatic notes, but doublet notes from two recensions, lacunae and Greek quotations need flagging
pilot_unit: Commentary on Adelphoe (est. 35–45k words); a smaller pilot is the preface plus Adelphoe Act 1 (~8k words)
